title: Part Three, Chapter 8: The Gods Hidden Away

verses.t: And then Tohil, with Avilix and Hacavitz, said to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, "Let us go; let us rise up from here! We must not stay here. Put us in a hidden and secret place, for the dawn has drawn near. Would it not be a misfortune for you if we were seized and taken captive by enemies in this building where you now keep us, you honoured ones? And put us in separate places." This is what he said when he spoke. "Very well," they said, "we shall pull up from here and look for forests," they all said. And then they took up their gods on their backs, each of them; and Avilix was carried to a ravine which is called by us the ravine of the hiding place, a great ravine in the forest which is now called At Avilix; and there he stayed; he was left in the ravine by Balam-acab; and they left them one after another. The first to be left was Hacavitz, above a great river called Red Water, and the mountain is now called Hacavitz; and there was his dwelling, and there the god Hacavitz stayed, for that was his name. And likewise Mahucutah stayed with his god, who was the second to be hidden by them. Hacavitz was not in a forest, but was hidden on a bare, open mountain. And then Balam-quitzé came and arrived there at a great forest to hide Tohil, whom Balam-quitzé hid; and that forest is now called Patohil. And they celebrated the hiding in the ravine, the guardian place of Tohil; and many snakes and many jaguars, vipers and cantí snakes are there in the ravine and the forest where they were hidden by those lords and chiefs. And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were all together, and together they waited for the dawn on the mountain called Hacavitz. And there was a short distance from where the gods of Tanub and Ylocab were: Amactan was the name of the place where the god of Tanub was, and there the dawn came for the peoples; and there the dawn came for those of Ylocab, where the god of Ylocab was, there being a short distance from one place to the other. And all the Rabinals were there, the Cakchiquels, those of Quiquinaha, all the peoples, small and great; and together they stood waiting for the dawn and for the rising of the morning star, which rises first before the sun when it dawns. And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were all together, and they kept watch without sleeping, and great was the weeping of their hearts for the dawn and the light to come. And likewise they were ashamed there, and great sadness and lamentation came upon them, and they were undone with grief. And they stayed there and said, "Woe to us! Bitterly have we come. Alas, we came to see the dawn, and it does not dawn! What are we to do, when all are in the same plight? Our faces were all alike in our homeland, and we have been forsaken!" This is what they said, speaking with one another in that sadness and lamentation and weeping. And they said, "Our hearts are not at peace about the rising of the sun. And now our gods are put away in the ravines and the forests, in the weeds and the moss; they did not put them on good seats of planks," they said. And that Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz are great things, and of great power over all the gods of the peoples; they are great, and many are their wonders and miracles on the journeys, in the wet and the cold; and their being strikes fear into the hearts of the peoples. And the minds of Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were calm and at rest; yet they seemed despairing about the god they had carried when they came from Tulanzú, from there in the East. And now they are in the forest which is now called and is named: the dawning at Tohil, at Avilix and at Hacavitz. And now we shall tell of when our grandfathers and fathers were sown and brought into light, and when it grew bright and the face of the sun, the moon and the stars was seen.
